prior_v1_findings_adjudication.summary: Unified V2 Modal app (coliee-pipeline-v2-embed-m3-opt-v2) handles both document and query embeddings, guarded by a mandatory real compatibility preflight (8 document checks + 3 query checks against baseline vectors/app).

PersistentBM25.create() strips 'text' before storing documents.metadata, streams postings in bounded 512-row batches (one Counter in RAM at a time), and batches metadata retrieval via get_many(..., 256). SQLite size dropped from 138,936,320 to 93,270,016 bytes (-32.87%) and case BM25 search dropped from ~0.31s to 0.0225s (~13.8x faster).

FastSession.__init__() no longer preloads all passage metadata or scans all vector norms/finiteness on open (full vector scan is reserved for verify(full_db=True)). Local CLI commands (build, verify, open, --help) neither parse .env nor import modal, and verify/open do not write operation files to the runtime directory.
PersistentBM25 resolves relative paths via Path(path).resolve() before constructing readonly file URIs.

Benchmark sampling now uses 4 locally dense contiguous windows of 64 passages each (256 unique IDs, 33,801 input tokens/pass) shared across candidate batch sizes [16, 32, 64] over 3 counterbalanced crossover repeats, with 128 isolated as a separate memory stress test. Padding ratios are bounded at 1.028 (bs=16), 1.056 (bs=32), and 1.121 (bs=64), revealing batch_size=64 as the fastest observed warm client candidate (23.00 docs/s).

Timings are cleanly separated across subprocess walltime (6.34-6.59s), internal full_cli_seconds (6.15-6.38s), session_initialization_seconds (0.56-0.61s), warm_session_request_seconds_including_RPC (2.90-5.53s), client_rpc_seconds (2.11-4.40s), remote_total_seconds (0.055-0.305s), and local_vector_reuse_seconds (0.174-0.264s, mean 0.208s).

findings.title: PyTorch CUDA caching allocator retains peak_reserved_bytes (20.56 GB) from stress-128 across subsequent warm benchmark calls on the same container
findings.evidence: In Engine.encode() (line 57), torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats() resets peak counters before each forward pass, while torch.cuda.empty_cache() is only called on OutOfMemoryError (line 77). Because stress-128 succeeded without OOM and reserved 20,560,478,208 bytes (86.79% of 23.69 GB L4 VRAM), PyTorch's caching allocator held onto that 20.56 GB reserved pool during all 84 subsequent warm calls for batch sizes 16, 32, and 64. Consequently, reserved_headroom_fraction is reported as 0.13208 (13.21%) for all three candidate sizes [16, 32, 64] in benchmark_result.json, whereas their true isolated reserved VRAM from stress-16/32/64 was 9.36 GB (60.49% headroom), 10.96 GB (53.74% headroom), and 14.16 GB (40.23% headroom).
findings.impact: Does not affect eligibility or winner selection (which gates on allocated_headroom_fraction >= 0.10, where 16/32/64 accurately report 63.36%, 61.00%, and 56.22% headroom), nor does it cause any OOM. However, readers inspecting reserved_headroom_fraction on warm calls should use the pre-128 stress-16/32/64 receipts for per-batch-size reserved memory.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional for future benchmarks: call torch.cuda.empty_cache() before torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats() in stress/benchmark mode, or compute per-candidate reserved_headroom_fraction from that candidate's own stress call when warm calls follow a larger stress batch.

findings.title: Full-corpus (415,693 passages / 7,708 cases) runner, COLIEE gold evaluation, and M4 agent remain intentionally out of pilot scope
findings.evidence: As documented in docs/M3_OPTIMIZATION_V2.md, m3.json remains locked to mode='pilot_only' (1,024 passages, 916 cases), and benchmark_result.json / search_benchmark.json explicitly record full_corpus_executed=false and status='PASS_components_measured_not_full_corpus_quality'.
findings.impact: The V2 architecture fixes (text-free SQLite metadata, streamed postings, lazy mmap/metadata session init, unified V2 Modal app with compatibility gate, and dense-window benchmark) are verified on the 1,024-passage pilot, but full-corpus index build/embedding and COLIEE F1 evaluation require their dedicated next-phase runner.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep pilot artifacts frozen; proceed to full-corpus runner design when scheduled by the project plan.
